_about: Exercise -> muscle contribution, for counting hard sets per muscle per week. Keyed on the Garmin catalog identity from models/exercises.py so it joins to prescriptions and synced workouts. Maintained alongside the Coach's knowledge files; attribution changes are proposed by the science agent and approved by the lifter.
_how_lookup_works: Most specific wins: 'CATEGORY:NAME' first, then 'CATEGORY'. A category default makes the whole movement pattern scorable; name entries exist only where a variant differs materially from its category. No match at any level is an explicit warning, never a silent zero.
_contribution_scale: 1.0 = a hard set of this exercise counts as a full hard set for that muscle; 0.5 = half; 0.25 = minor. Fractional set counting, as used in the volume dose-response literature. These are informed judgements, not measured coefficients.

vocabulary.glute_med: gluteus medius/minimus — hip abduction and pelvic stability; NOT interchangeable with glute_max
vocabulary.hamstrings: hamstrings — knee flexion and hip extension
vocabulary.erectors: spinal erectors and the rest of the posterior trunk
vocabulary.lats: latissimus dorsi — shoulder extension and adduction
vocabulary.mid_back: rhomboids and mid trapezius — scapular retraction
vocabulary.abs: rectus abdominis and deep trunk flexors
vocabulary.hip_flexors: iliopsoas and rectus femoris as a hip flexor

evidence_notes.SQUAT:glute_max: Back squat counts as a FULL hard set for glute max. Plotkin et al. 2023 found squat and hip thrust produced equivalent glute hypertrophy by MRI over nine weeks despite the hip thrust's much larger acute EMG signal — in untrained participants. Acute EMG amplitude is not a hypertrophy ranking. Omitting squat undercounts glute volume.
evidence_notes.HIP_STABILITY:glute_med: Abduction work trains glute medius/minimus, NOT glute max. Pooling the two inflates a weekly glute-max count; for a goal that depends on glute max they are not interchangeable.
evidence_notes.SQUAT:LEG_PRESS: Held at 0.5 for glute max deliberately. A 2025 review reported high glute growth for leg press, but those percentages come from separate studies with different protocols and measures and do not form a valid head-to-head ranking against hip thrust or squat.
evidence_notes.leg_extension: There is no QUAD leg-extension machine in the Garmin catalog. The names that exist are BANDED_EXERCISES:LEG_EXTENSION (a banded movement) and CRUNCH:LEG_EXTENSIONS / CRUNCH:WEIGHTED_LEG_EXTENSIONS, which are ABDOMINAL exercises (lying leg extensions), filed under CRUNCH and correctly mapped to abs here. Do NOT remap them to quads — that would corrupt the map for anyone using them as intended. A campaign that prescribes a quad leg-extension machine under one of these names is mis-identified at the source and scores as abdominal volume; its zero glute-max contribution stays visible either way.
evidence_notes.banded_and_total_body: BANDED_EXERCISES, TOTAL_BODY, SUSPENSION, SANDBAG, SLED, TIRE, BATTLE_ROPE and LADDER have no category default on purpose: their contents span the whole body, so any default would be wrong more often than right. They warn as unmapped until a specific variant is added.
